summary: Mun-keat Choong is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA ~1986–1990), and the University of Queensland, earning an MA (~1992–1994) supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell and a PhD (~1994–1998).

Munenobu Sakurai specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1984–1989) and held posts as assistant professor at Iwate University and professor at Tohoku University (attested 2005).

Muneo Tokunaga was an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1969–1971) and Harvard University (PhD ~1974–1982). He served as assistant professor at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1981–1988) and at Kyoto University (~1988–1990), where he was later professor (~1990–2008).
Mungunchimeg Batmunkh works in Tibetology, religious studies, and other fields. She earned a Dr.phil. from the University of Vienna (attested 2010), supervised by Brigitte Marschall.

Murray Barnson Emeneau worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Dalhousie University (~1919–1923), Balliol College (~1923–1935), and Yale University under Franklin Edgerton (PhD 1926–1931). In 1940, he became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

Musashi Tachikawa specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned doctorates from Harvard (1967–1975) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Nagoya University (1960–1985). He held posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and other institutions.

Muzaffar Alam works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he taught (~1973–2001) before joining the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College Dublin (~1917–1922). He held academic posts at Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1949–1972).
Myoshin Fujitake is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and as a committee member of the Otani Society (attested 2000).
Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912–1927) and at the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).
Myōsei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as professor (attested 1987) and later professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.
Mónika Kiss is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She pursued doctoral studies in Japanese studies at Eötvös Loránd University under the advisorship of Masanori Yamaji.
N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

N. Veezhinathan is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University (-1964) under A. Sankaran. After researching at Deccan College (1960–1963), he became a lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Ferrand Edward Corley. He served as Reader at the University of Madras and Deputy Director for Epigraphy for the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
Nagin J. Shah is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as Acting Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968), succeeding Dalsukh D. Malvania.

Nalinaksha Dutt worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Chittagong College, the University of Calcutta (PhD ~1918–1921), and the University of London (DLitt ~1921–1924), later heading the Department of Pali at Calcutta.

Nalini Balbir is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat (~1976–1980). She held appointments at INALCO, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, becoming professor there around 2000.

Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. Supervised by Leslie Orr, she earned a PhD from Concordia University (attested 2004) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2004).

Nam-lin Hur is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history who studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton (PhD under Helen Hardacre). He was a Harvard postdoctoral fellow and became professor of Japanese history and religious culture at UBC.
